messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: ftemplate-depth again
parts:
Can some Mac person resolve a question for me ASAP so that I can upload rstan to CRAN?

The default compilers for Mac

http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html

are llvm-g++-4.2 for Snow Leopard, clang++ based on Xcode 5.1 on Mavericks, and clang++ based on Xcode 6.0 on Yosemite (or whatever 10.10 is).

We added the -ftemplate-depth=256 option to Stan

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/278

because Xcode 5.0 defaults to 128.

However, CRAN deems -ftemplate-depth non-portable

http://win-builder.r-project.org/2o50ctRVx8Ip/00check.log

So, there are a few options
  • Does Xcode 5.1 still default to 128? I suspect Xcode 6.x does not because the C++11 standard requires 1024. Maybe we can git rid of -ftemplate-depth now.
  • Is the template depth issue only for compiling stanc or does it also come up in models? I can have rstan build under the C++11 standard in which case we should be okay to build stanc, but Mac users with Xcode 5.1 may have to add -ftemplate-depth=256 to their ~/.R/Makevars to build models. And we would not be able to build a CRAN binary for Snow Leopard.
  • Remove -ftemplate-depth from the rstan Makevars, in which case we would not be able to build a CRAN binary for Mavericks but Mavericks users could install the rstan package from source if -ftemplate-depth=256 is added to their ~/.R/Makevars
  • Argue with CRAN about whether -ftemplate-depth is sufficiently portable.
  • ???

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ftemplate-depth again
parts:
Actually we added -ftemplate-depth-256, not -ftemplate-depth=256. I think old
gcc does not support the latter, so it is not portable.

I think we can get rid of it now. My impression is that there is only one version
of Xcode that set the depth to 128. From your lists, that version of xcode
would not be used. So it would not be a problem to remove it.

Jiqiang
